notes: Every report now opens on an executive summary: the pack's purpose, what the findings show, a count for each section and the most serious items, filling one or two pages.
Each run writes a paragraph on what the findings show taken together and points to weigh before deciding, and a second check confirms every sentence before it prints.
Investment Due Diligence ends its summary by saying the report sets out evidence from the code and is not advice on whether to invest.
A long list of folders now shows five, with every folder listed in an appendix, and no status label on a report wraps onto a second line.
A new pack checks your code against the Australian Information Security Manual, September 2026 edition.
Where a check finds no document a requirement asks for, the fix now says to include the folder that holds your documentation when you start the next check.
Every report, question and message now follows one writing standard, with spelling and dates that match your locale.
The status "No evidence" is now called Environment, meaning a control that can be set outside the code, such as in your hosting platform, where this run saw nothing.
The licence scan can look up the licences of dependencies it couldn't read locally, after you agree to send only the list of package names.
Reviews check each answer again before keeping it, and long reviews no longer stall on a large batch of claims.
The question about your company's email domains now says why it asks, and to add the addresses of staff using personal accounts and of consultants whose work you own.
A review with long packs, such as Investment Due Diligence, no longer stops partway through reading.
Error reports sent to us now say more clearly what we need to change. Nothing you see changes.
When something in Evalation goes wrong, the report it sends us now says what we need to change to fix it. It still never sends your code, paths or repository names.
A review no longer stops when your repository's history shows no company email address. It asks you to type your company's domains.
Error reports now also leave out the names of the folders you work in.
When something in Evalation goes wrong, it now tells us, so we can fix it without you having to. It never sends your code, paths or repository names.
Warnings about an old copy or a branch other than main now show cleanly, with no failed steps.
A review of several repositories now opens cleanly, with no stray counts or failed steps.
Every command now starts by saying what it does.
Every question set now extends a pack. A set saved without one asks you to pick its pack before a run can use it.
Questions taken from a website or a document extend the Investment pack.
Long lists fill each screen before moving to the next.
When a review asks which email addresses belong to your company, your own sign-in comes first, and you can name whole addresses as well as domains.
A question you can leave empty now says to press Skip to choose none.
Saving a question set ends on one plain line telling you how to use it.
Question sets now start by asking what you'd like to do, and you can delete a set you no longer need.
Your account now tells you your balance once, in the question to buy more, and no longer lists your packs.
Writing a new question set no longer fails when an earlier attempt left a draft behind.
Every message and question is shorter and plainer.
The note that a newer version is out now reads as a plain line from the command, without a label in front of it.
When a newer version is out, you're told in one line, however many versions behind you are.
Each requirement in a question set now reads as the requirement alone, without a note on how it's checked.
When your questions are checked, you're told only about changes to the questions you wrote, each by its title and once.
A requirement that names what your question asks about, such as a list of the third party scripts for a question about them, is now kept.
While your questions are checked, you're told so once, and each question's title once as it passes.
Writing your own questions no longer asks your permission to read or write Evalation's own draft files.
In a list you tick, ticking nothing now means none from that list, and the command carries on.
Tick lists no longer offer a None of these answer.
Skipping a question in one Claude Code window no longer stops Evalation from saving your answers in another.
When you write your own questions, you're asked which pack they should extend, and offered only the packs they can extend.
If you type a published standard such as SOC 2 there, it says what your questions can go with and asks again.
When you skip a question, the command now stops, saves nothing from it and waits for you to say what to do next.
When a run asks whether to read copies more than 14 days old, you can now talk it through before you choose.
You can buy pack credits from /ev-account. It opens Stripe's payment page, and nothing is charged until you pay there.
A clause that places no duty your code could meet now shows as does not apply, with the reason.
The first Evalation command in a session tells you when a newer version is out, and what's in it.
When your organisation has to approve you or a new machine, Evalation tells you who approves it and what to do next.
Signing in asks which company you're using Evalation for, so a consultant can name their client.
The licence check now reads Rust crates too, from the copies already downloaded on your machine.
The investment pack looks at five more working habits in your commit history, such as how often commits name a ticket.
A new licence check finds production dependencies whose licence could make you share your own code.
A report that names the people who committed to your code says so on its first page.
Someone who commits from two addresses now counts as one person, and bots aren't counted at all.
Every message and question now reads the same way each time you run a command.
When something fails, you see one plain line, and the details go in a file you can send to support.
Removing Evalation deletes only its own folder and the conversations that ran an Evalation command.
